title: Vessel Condition Survey for Owners, Charterers and Lenders
description: Vessel condition surveys for owners, charterers and financiers: structure, coatings rated GOOD, FAIR or POOR, thickness, machinery and ranked defects.
h1: Vessel condition survey: an independent assessment of a ship in service
intro: A vessel condition survey gives an owner, charterer or financier an independent picture of a ship in service, on the client's timetable rather than the class survey cycle. Atlantis NDT surveys structure and tanks space by space, rates coatings in the IACS GOOD, FAIR and POOR terms, takes spot thickness readings and crack checks, and measures machinery while it runs. The report rates each area, ranks defects by priority and compares the ship with earlier reports. Teams are mobilised from India to the vessel.

highlights.h: On your timetable, not the class cycle
highlights.p: The survey is commissioned when a decision needs evidence: a fleet review, a charter, a loan, a docking plan, an incident or a sale. The scope follows that purpose, so a lender's review and a docking plan look at the same ship through different questions.

highlights.h: The same rating language every time
highlights.p: Coatings are rated GOOD, FAIR or POOR as defined in the IACS hull survey requirements, and structure and machinery on a written scale of our own, so a fleet surveyed over several years can be compared area by area and ship by ship.

Each defect is located, photographed and placed in one of three priorities: act now, act by the next survey or docking, or keep watching. The master and the technical manager hear about the first group before the team leaves the ship.

sections.h: What a vessel condition survey is, and how it differs from CAS and CAP
p: A vessel condition survey is a commercial survey commissioned by the owner, a charterer or a financier to establish the actual state of a ship in service. No rule requires it, it carries no class or flag status, and its scope is whatever the purpose needs.

Two schemes with similar names work differently, and both are explained on their own pages here. The IMO Condition Assessment Scheme (CAS) is statutory: it applies to older single-hull oil tankers, is carried out by a recognised organisation's surveyors and ends in a Statement of Compliance from the flag Administration. A Condition Assessment Programme (CAP) is a voluntary class service in which the classification society surveys the ship to its own procedure and issues a rating that charterers read. A vessel condition survey borrows their discipline, space-by-space inspection, coating ratings and measured thickness, without their formal process, and it sits outside the class survey cycle altogether.

sections.h: When owners, charterers and financiers commission one
p: The purpose decides where the survey looks hardest. After an incident, the class damage survey stays with the classification society, which the owner must notify; our survey is the owner's own record and runs alongside it. Before a recycling decision, the Inventory of Hazardous Materials page covers the other survey that question raises.

p: A full survey takes in the whole ship; a narrower one takes the areas its purpose names. Each space is entered where it is safe and permitted, and each system is seen running where the ship can run it. Safety items are visual observations only, with no certification and no substitute for a statutory survey. The Ship Piping Inspection and Hatch Cover Ultrasonic Tightness Testing pages cover those parts of the scope in depth.

sections.h: How condition is rated: IACS coating terms and a priority scale
p: Coatings are rated in the terms IACS UR Z7 defines, which class surveyors and charterers already read. A coating is GOOD when it shows only minor spot rusting; FAIR when it has broken down locally at stiffener edges and weld connections, or shows light rusting on a fifth or more of the area under consideration without reaching POOR; and POOR when it has broken down generally on a fifth or more of that area, or carries hard scale on a tenth or more. A POOR rating in a ballast tank of an enhanced survey programme ship brings class back to that tank at each annual survey, so the word carries weight beyond our report.
Structure, closing appliances and machinery are rated on a written three-step scale, applied the same way on every ship and issued with the report, and every defect is placed in one priority group.

p: The readings in a condition survey are a structured sample, not a renewal-survey gauging. Points are chosen where each space is most likely to be losing steel, recorded on a sketch by frame and member, and kept so the next survey measures the same points. Each reading is compared with the original thickness and the class allowable; where an earlier report exists, the change gives a corrosion rate for that point. Hatch corners, bracket toes, side longitudinal connections and crane pedestals are examined visually, and with magnetic particle testing where the surface can be cleaned.

A gauging that class can credit to a renewal survey is a different job: IACS UR Z17 requires the firm taking it to hold approval from the ship's own classification society. Atlantis is in the process of obtaining UR Z17 approval from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS, and until a certificate is issued its condition survey readings support the owner's planning, not a class survey.

sections.h: Machinery readings: a snapshot, and when to trend instead
p: Machinery is assessed while it runs, so the visit is timed for a port call or passage where the chief engineer can put generators, pumps, compressors, fans and purifiers on load. Vibration on bearings and casings is measured overall and as a spectrum, and judged against the evaluation guidance of ISO 20816-1 and against identical machines on board. Switchboards, motor starters and exhaust lagging are surveyed with a thermal camera, as described on the Infrared Thermography page. Planned maintenance records show what readings cannot: overdue overhauls, repeated defects and postponed jobs.

One survey shows what is wrong on the day, not how fast a bearing or a connection is deteriorating. Owners who want the rate move from a single survey to the Condition Monitoring service, which revisits fixed points at intervals set by the trading pattern.

The report opens with the overall condition, the Priority 1 items and the decisions the client faces. It then works area by area: hull envelope, cargo spaces, ballast tanks, deck and closing appliances, deck machinery, engine room, electrical equipment and safety observations, each with its rating, defects and photographs taken from recorded positions so the next survey can repeat the view.

Where an earlier condition or thickness report exists, ours or another firm's, each area shows whether condition has improved, held or worsened, and the readings appendix lists earlier and new values point by point. If a charterer, lender or fleet department has its own format, send it before the survey and the findings are presented in it.

sections.h: When a P&I club, an insurer or a charterer sends its own surveyor
p: P&I clubs often survey older ships when they enter the club, hull and machinery insurers sometimes call for a condition survey, and charterers appoint surveyors for on-hire and off-hire. Our survey replaces none of them: each party relies on its own surveyor. What an owner's survey does is give the owner the evidence first. Defects found weeks before another surveyor boards can be put right or documented, and an owner holding a measured record of holds and tanks at delivery is better placed if damage is disputed at redelivery.

Every survey is carried out by a team mobilised from India. Atlantis keeps no office or agent at any port, so the visit is fitted to the ship's itinerary and the time visas take, and the ship's agent handles port entry. Planning and supervision sit with the founder, our Responsible NDT Level III, whose ASNT NDT Level III covers UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and who brings more than eleven years of international field experience. Technicians are qualified under the company's written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, analysts and thermographers measure vibration and heat to written procedures, and the company is ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 certified.

faqs.q: Is a vessel condition survey the same as a CAP or a CAS survey?
faqs.a: No. CAS is the IMO's statutory scheme for older single-hull oil tankers, carried out by a recognised organisation, and CAP is a voluntary rating issued by a classification society to its own procedure. A vessel condition survey is a commercial survey: the scope is agreed with the client, no class rating results, and the report belongs to whoever commissioned it.

faqs.q: How often should a ship have a condition survey?
faqs.a: No rule sets it. Owners who use condition surveys as a fleet tool often survey each ship yearly, or between the intermediate and renewal surveys so the docking specification rests on recent evidence. Otherwise the survey follows events: a new charter, a redelivery, a loan, an incident or a decision to sell. The more regular the interval, the more the comparison with the last report tells you.

faqs.q: Can the survey be done while the ship is trading?
faqs.a: Most of it can. Ballast tanks are entered when empty and certified safe, holds after discharge, and decks, closing appliances and machinery at a normal port call or anchorage. A tanker's cargo tanks are rarely gas-free in service and the external bottom needs a drydock, so those are assessed from records and the readings that can be taken. The report lists every space not entered.

faqs.q: Can the survey readings be used for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: Not as class gauging. Class accepts thickness readings for a survey only from a firm its own society has approved under IACS UR Z17, and Atlantis is still working towards UR Z17 approval from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS. A condition survey is a sound way to plan the renewal survey, though: it shows where the class gauging will find wastage, early enough to plan the steel work before the yard writes its specification.

faqs.q: Does an owner's condition survey replace the P&I club's survey?
faqs.a: No. A club, an insurer or a charterer appoints its own surveyor and relies on that surveyor's report. An owner's survey gives the owner the facts first: time to repair or document defects before the other surveyor boards, and a measured record of condition that can be produced if a later report disagrees with it. The two reports serve different parties.

faqs.q: What do you need from us before the survey?
faqs.a: Start with the ship's IMO number and what the survey is for, then the port, dates and expected cargo condition, the class survey status, earlier condition and thickness reports, the structural drawings or midship section if you have them, and any report format required. Visas for a team travelling from India take time, so the earlier the port is known the better. Write to info@atlantisndt.com or use the enquiry form.
